name: Word Analogies
blurb: The first two words go together. Make the next two match.
childIntro: The first two words go together in some way. Find the word that makes the second pair go together the same way.
howItWorks: A is to B as C is to what. It runs at OLSAT levels D through G. The relationships used are the same family as on CogAT: opposites, part and whole, tool and user, object and function.
parentTip: A recurring OLSAT trick is a word with the right meaning but the wrong part of speech. Near is to far as light is to distance fails because distance is a noun where an adjective is needed. Ask your child whether the answer word is the same KIND of word as the one it replaces.

questions.prompt: Scissors is to cut as straw is to —
questions.explanation: Scissors are for cutting. A straw is for drinking. Plastic is what a straw is made of and water is what goes through it, but neither is what it is FOR.
questions.strategy: Object and its job. Ask what it is for.

questions.prompt: Puppy is to dog as kitten is to —
questions.explanation: A puppy grows into a dog. A kitten grows into a cat. Fur, milk and mice are all things linked to cats without being what a kitten becomes.
questions.strategy: Baby and grown up. Every animal has both names.

questions.prompt: Hot is to cold as day is to —
questions.explanation: Hot and cold are opposites. So the answer must be the opposite of day, which is night. Morning is a part of a day and a week is a group of days.
questions.strategy: When the first pair are opposites, look only for opposites.

questions.prompt: Painter is to brush as writer is to —
questions.explanation: A painter works with a brush. A writer works with a pen. A book and a story are what a writer produces, not the tool.
questions.strategy: Worker and tool. Do not pick the finished product.

questions.prompt: Near is to far as narrow is to —
questions.explanation: Near and far are opposites. The opposite of narrow is wide. Choice c, width, means roughly the right thing but it is a naming word where a describing word is needed. Choice b, thin, means the same as narrow.
questions.strategy: Match the kind of word. If the first three are describing words, so is the answer.

questions.prompt: Bird is to feather as fish is to —
questions.explanation: A feather is what covers a bird's body. A scale is what covers a fish's body. Fins and gills are parts of a fish but they are not the covering.
questions.strategy: Match the exact part, not just any part.

questions.prompt: Library is to books as museum is to —
questions.explanation: A library is a place that holds books. A museum is a place that holds exhibits. Visitors go there, tickets get you in, and history is the subject, but none of those is what the building holds.
questions.strategy: Place and what it stores. Ask what is on the shelves.

questions.prompt: Herd is to cattle as swarm is to —
questions.explanation: A herd is a group of cattle. A swarm is a group of bees. Honey, hives, stings and flowers are all connected to bees without being what the group is made of.
questions.strategy: Group words always point at the animal they gather: herd, flock, swarm, pack, school.

questions.prompt: Drought is to water as famine is to —
questions.explanation: A drought is a shortage of water. A famine is a shortage of food. Hunger is the result of a famine, and crops are one source of food, but the pair is about what is missing.
questions.strategy: Some pairs mean a shortage of something. Ask what is running out.

questions.prompt: Whisper is to shout as drizzle is to —
questions.explanation: A whisper is a small amount of sound and a shout is a large amount. A drizzle is a small amount of rain and a downpour is a large amount. Choice b, rain, is the general word, not the big end. Choice e, storm, adds wind and thunder, which the pair does not.
questions.strategy: Some pairs go from a little to a lot of the very same thing. Match the amount exactly.

questions.prompt: Pen is to write as knife is to —
questions.explanation: A pen is for writing. A knife is for cutting. Sharp describes a knife and metal is what it is made of, but neither is its job.
questions.strategy: Object and its job. Ask what it is FOR.

questions.prompt: Foot is to sock as hand is to —
questions.explanation: A sock goes on a foot. A glove goes on a hand. A finger is part of a hand and a ring goes on a finger, but the glove covers the whole hand just as the sock covers the whole foot.
questions.strategy: Match the covering to the body part it covers.

questions.prompt: Loud is to quiet as heavy is to —
questions.explanation: Loud and quiet are opposites, so the answer must be the opposite of heavy, which is light. Strong and solid are not about weight.
questions.strategy: When the first pair are opposites, look only for opposites.

questions.prompt: Bee is to hive as rabbit is to —
questions.explanation: A bee lives in a hive. A rabbit lives in a burrow. A carrot is what it eats, hopping is what it does, and a field is where it might be found, but the burrow is its home.
questions.strategy: Home, food and action are three different relationships.

questions.prompt: Baker is to bread as farmer is to —
questions.explanation: A baker makes bread. A farmer grows crops. A tractor is a tool, a barn is a building and a field is a place. Only crops are what the farmer produces.
questions.strategy: Worker and what they produce. Not the tool and not the place.

questions.prompt: Petal is to flower as page is to —
questions.explanation: A petal is one part of a flower. A page is one part of a book. Paper is what a page is made of and a library is where books live.
questions.strategy: Part and whole. Go from the small piece up to the thing it belongs to.

questions.prompt: Chick is to hen as calf is to —
questions.explanation: A chick grows into a hen. A calf grows into a cow. Milk comes from a cow and grass is what it eats. A bull is the male, not what the calf grows into.
questions.strategy: Baby to grown-up. Make sure you match the same one, male or female.

questions.prompt: Second is to minute as inch is to —
questions.explanation: Sixty seconds make a minute. Twelve inches make a foot. A ruler measures inches and length is the general idea, but only a foot is the next unit up.
questions.strategy: Units of measurement stack. Find the next size up.

questions.prompt: Smile is to happy as frown is to —
questions.explanation: A smile shows you are happy. A frown shows you are sad. Crying is another thing a sad person does, but a frown is a face, and the pair matches a face to the feeling behind it.
questions.strategy: Match the sign to the feeling it shows.

questions.prompt: Sip is to gulp as tap is to —
questions.explanation: A sip is a small drink and a gulp is a big one. A tap is a small hit and a pound is a big one. Both pairs go from a little to a lot of the same thing. Knocking is closer to tapping in size.
questions.strategy: Some pairs are about strength. Find the small and the large version.

questions.prompt: Author is to novel as sculptor is to —
questions.explanation: An author makes a novel. A sculptor makes a statue. Marble is the material, a chisel is the tool and a gallery is where it is shown.
questions.strategy: Maker and the thing made. Not the tool and not the material.

questions.prompt: Thermometer is to temperature as scale is to —
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature. A scale measures weight. A kilogram is a unit of weight, so it is one step too specific, and measure is the general idea.
questions.strategy: Match the general thing measured, not a unit of it.

questions.prompt: Cub is to bear as fawn is to —
questions.explanation: A cub is a young bear. A fawn is a young deer. A doe is an adult female deer, so it is close, but deer is the animal itself.
questions.strategy: Baby animals have their own names. Learn them in pairs.

questions.prompt: Island is to ocean as oasis is to —
questions.explanation: An island is a patch of land surrounded by ocean. An oasis is a patch of water surrounded by desert. Sand is what a desert is made of and a camel lives there.
questions.strategy: Look for the pattern of one thing surrounded by another, even when they swap places.

questions.prompt: Famine is to food as drought is to —
questions.explanation: A famine is a shortage of food. A drought is a shortage of water. Heat causes a drought and thirst is the result of one.
questions.strategy: Shortage pairs. Ask what is running out.

questions.prompt: Chapter is to book as movement is to —
questions.explanation: A chapter is a named section of a book. A movement is a named section of a symphony. An orchestra plays it and music is the general idea.
questions.strategy: Part and whole works for time-based things too, not just objects.

questions.prompt: Whisper is to shout as glimpse is to —
questions.explanation: A whisper is a small amount of sound and a shout is a large amount. A glimpse is a very short look and a stare is a long one. Glance means the same as glimpse.
questions.strategy: Match the amount as well as the meaning. Small to large.

questions.prompt: Cartographer is to map as architect is to —
questions.explanation: A cartographer makes maps. An architect designs buildings. A blueprint is the drawing they work from, and a brick is a material.
questions.strategy: When one word is unfamiliar, use the second half of the pair to work out the relationship.

questions.prompt: Optimist is to hopeful as pessimist is to —
questions.explanation: An optimist is a person who is hopeful. A pessimist is a person who is gloomy. The pair matches a kind of person to the feeling that describes them. Realistic is a different attitude altogether.
questions.strategy: Match a person to the word that describes their outlook.

questions.prompt: Trickle is to torrent as spark is to —
questions.explanation: A trickle is a tiny flow of water and a torrent is a huge one. A spark is a tiny fire and a blaze is a huge one. A flame sits in between, and smoke is a by-product.
questions.strategy: Both pairs go from the smallest version to the largest. Match the extreme.
